label: lf-test-labs
topic: Who can fire-test a small bio-based coating sample (cone calorimeter, E84 tunnel, SBI), and open cone-calorimeter data that could stand in for a lab
summary: Partial result in about 7 minutes: five pages opened and read, the rest is search-snippet only and marked as such. Only one provider (Measurlabs, a Finnish testing broker) publishes prices and sample sizes: cone calorimeter ISO 5660-1 at 928 EUR per sample plus a 97 EUR order fee, needing 6 pieces of 100 mm x 100 mm; SBI EN 13823 at 1,978 EUR per sample, needing 3-5 corner specimens 1.5 m tall. No page I opened states a testing lead time. In the US north-east, VTEC Laboratories (Bronx, NY) offers ASTM E1354 and says it is ISO 17025 accredited, with no price shown. WPI lists two cone calorimeters but its page says nothing about taking outside samples. I confirmed no UK university lab that takes outside samples. For open data, the NIST Fire Calorimetry Database appears (search snippet only) to hold large-scale tests rather than cone data; the MaCFP material database on GitHub (MIT licence) is the more likely open source of bench-scale data, but the page I opened showed only PMMA and Wood folders and did not itself mention cone calorimeter. Cheapest practical route for a coating: cone calorimeter (small 100 mm squares) rather than E84 (24 ft specimen) or SBI (1.5 m corner). key_claims: Only one provider found publishes prices: cone ISO 5660-1 at 928 EUR/sample and SBI EN 13823 at 1,978 EUR/sample (Measurlabs), each plus a 97 EUR order fee.
Cone calorimeter is the only one of the three tests that fits a small sample: six 100 mm squares versus a 1.5 m corner (SBI) or a 24 ft strip (E84, unverified snippet).
No opened page states a testing lead time.
US north-east: VTEC Laboratories (Bronx, NY) offers ASTM E1354 with self-stated ISO 17025 accreditation; WPI has two cone calorimeters but states no outside-sample service.
No UK university lab taking outside samples was confirmed.
NIST FCD looks like large-scale data only (unverified); MaCFP matl-db is the better open candidate but its cone content was not verified in the files.

recommendations: Treat the cone calorimeter (ISO 5660-1 / ASTM E1354) as the first test: six 100 mm squares, roughly 5,600 EUR at the one published rate (6 x 928 + 97, my arithmetic, assuming each piece is billed as a sample - the page does not say whether 'per sample' means per piece or per material).
Before relying on open data, inspect the MaCFP matl-db folders for cone calorimeter files and check the NIST FCD landing page directly; neither was verified here.

A follow-up agent should read the UKAS schedules (0249, 0578, 27297) with a PDF text extractor to confirm which UK labs hold EN 13823 and ISO 5660-1 in scope, and check Ulster, Edinburgh and UCLan pages for outside-sample terms.
Lead times and E84 prices are not public on the pages reached; they would need a quote request, which this task forbids.
lay_summary: To show a new coating is safe in a fire, a lab burns pieces of it and measures how much heat and smoke come off.
The smallest test needs only six squares about the size of a coaster, and one company lists it at about 928 euros per sample.
The bigger tests need a piece as tall as a door or as long as a bus, so they cost more and need much more material.
We found a lab in New York that does the small test and a university in Massachusetts that owns the machines, but neither says its price or how long it takes.
There is some free burn-test data online, but we could not confirm it has the right kind of test for a coating.

glossary.cone calorimeter: A bench-top machine that heats a small flat sample with a cone-shaped heater and measures how much heat and smoke it gives off as it burns.
glossary.ISO 5660-1 / ASTM E1354: The international and American written rules for how to run a cone calorimeter test.
glossary.ASTM E84 (tunnel test): An American test that burns a long strip of material along the ceiling of a tunnel to see how fast flame spreads and how much smoke is made.
glossary.ASTM D3806: A small 2-foot version of the tunnel test used to screen fire-retardant paints.
glossary.SBI / EN 13823: Single Burning Item: a European test that burns a room-corner-shaped specimen to rate building products.
glossary.accredited: Checked by an official body to confirm the lab runs a test properly.
glossary.ISO 17025: The international standard a testing lab is checked against to be called accredited.
glossary.UKAS: The United Kingdom's official body that accredits labs; its 'schedule' lists exactly which tests a lab is approved for.
glossary.specimen: One piece of material prepared for a test.
glossary.lead time: How long you wait between sending a sample and getting results.
glossary.heat release rate: How fast a burning material gives off heat; the main number a cone calorimeter reports.
glossary.NIST FCD: Fire Calorimetry Database of the US National Institute of Standards and Technology, a public collection of fire experiment measurements.
glossary.MaCFP: Measurement and Computation of Fire Phenomena, a research group that shares burn-test data openly.
glossary.PMMA: Acrylic plastic (Perspex), a standard reference material in fire tests.
glossary.bio-based coating: A paint-like layer made from biological materials rather than petroleum.
glossary.MIT licence: A permissive licence that lets anyone reuse the data or code freely.
glossary.VAT: Value-added tax, a sales tax added to the listed price in Europe.
